latest_first_ordering: Phase 3b: (1) HEASARC fermigbrst live row = the newest team fits (Poolakkil+2021-era values, refreshed catalog) -> DEFAULT comparison frame for spectra; (2) von Kienlin+2020 (4th GBM catalog) -> durations/identity; (3) Ajello+2019 2FLGC -> LAT, and the ONLY refereed per-burst analysis; (4) Gruber+2014 / Bhat+2016 / von Kienlin+2014 -> superseded by (1) and kept only for lineage. No GCN circular exists, so the usual 'GCN is preliminary by its own statement' bottom rung is absent.
finding: A CATALOG-ONLY BURST THAT THE STANDARD HARVEST CANNOT SEE. Zero GCN circulars, zero ADS full-text hits across seven query forms - yet the burst is NOT unstudied: it has a full GBM catalog spectral record and four Fermi-LAT catalog rows, all reachable only through machine tables (local corpus PDF scan + HEASARC TAP + VizieR). Physically it is (a) a LONG burst, T90 = 254.9 s with T50 starting at 21.5 s, of which our stamped window covers only the first 50 s; (b) exceptionally HARD - catalog peak-flux CPL Ep = 7993 +/- 2513 keV and time-integrated Band beta = -1.644 +/- 0.043, i.e. no high-energy break constrained inside the GBM band - which is exactly why the archival production run railed Band Ep at its old 5 MeV cap in every block; (c) strongly hard-to-soft, the softening happening mostly AFTER our window (catalog CPL Ep 7993 keV at the peak vs 363 keV integrated over 255 s, same model family); and (d) LAT-flagged but LAT-blind in our window (theta = 109.7 deg, zero events in the downloaded file, like_gbm_ts = 0, detection confined to 3502-3908 s). No redshift, no afterglow, no time-resolved spectroscopy anywhere - our block-resolved fits will be the first.
